name: Data Compression and Storage Optimization
text:
# Data Compression and Storage Optimization

Also called: 3DGS Compression, Gaussian Splatting Storage Optimization

## Overview
This family of methods addresses the excessive memory footprint and storage requirements of [3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS)](#1174-3d-gaussian-splatting-3dgs.md) models, which typically consist of millions of Gaussian primitives with high-dimensional attributes [S1, S2, S3]. While standard 3DGS stores explicit per-Gaussian parameters, these optimization techniques reduce redundancy through various mechanisms: ASCII-based encoding for training I/O efficiency [S1], [sensitivity-aware vector clustering](#12167-sensitivity-aware-vector-clustering.md) for [quantization](#5935-quantization.md) [S2], and [hybrid representations](#11926-non-baked-models.md) using [hash grids](#936-hash-grids.md) and codebooks for inference [S3]. They differ from sibling methods like [Sorting and Rendering Pipeline Optimization](12180-sorting-and-rendering-pipeline-optimization.md) by focusing on data representation rather than rendering throughput, and from [Gaussian Representation and Truncation](12855-gaussian-representation-and-truncation.md) by employing structured [compression](#4-compression.md) rather than simple pruning.

## Shared principles
All methods in this family aim to reduce the size of the scene representation without significantly degrading rendering quality. They operate on the core 3DGS attributes: position, opacity, scale, rotation, and view-dependent color ([Spherical Harmonics](#5603-spherical-harmonics.md), SH). The shared goal is to replace high-precision, per-primitive storage with compact indices, shared structures, or lossy encodings. Common techniques include [vector quantization](#907-vector-quantization.md), codebook-based storage, and [spatial hashing](#5002-spatial-hashing.md). The methods assume the standard 3DGS differentiable rasterization pipeline remains unchanged, with the compression applied to the input data structures before rendering or during the [training loop](#4290-training-loop.md).

## Subtopics

### [ASCII-Based Data Compression](11820-ascii-based-data-compression.md)
Compresses floating-point and integer values into ASCII strings to accelerate training I/O. It targets the bottleneck of data transmission rather than final model size, achieving ~6% training speed improvement.

### [Sensitivity-Aware Vector Clustering](12167-sensitivity-aware-vector-clustering.md)
Reduces storage by clustering SH coefficients and geometric features into codebooks using a sensitivity-aware k-Means algorithm. It prioritizes parameters that significantly impact image quality, differing from standard post-training quantization by incorporating gradient-based sensitivity measures.

### [Compact 3D Gaussian Representation (C3DGS)](12927-compact-3d-gaussian-representation-c3dgs.md)
Achieves >25x compression by replacing per-Gaussian attributes with a shared hash-based grid for colors and a discrete codebook for geometry. It eliminates redundant primitives via [volume-based masking](#12710-gaussian-volume-mask.md), setting it apart by integrating spatial redundancy exploitation directly into the representation.

## Background
3D [Gaussian Splatting](#946-gaussian-splatting.md) was introduced by Kerbl et al. in 2023 [G]. The method's high fidelity comes at the cost of large model sizes, often exceeding several gigabytes for complex scenes. Subsequent research focused on optimizing this storage. ASCII-based compression was proposed to speed up the training process by reducing I/O overhead [S1]. Sensitivity-aware clustering was developed to enable efficient quantization by identifying critical parameters [S2]. [C3DGS](#12927-compact-3d-gaussian-representation-c3dgs.md) introduced a hybrid approach combining hash grids and codebooks to drastically reduce memory usage for real-time rendering [S3]. These methods are used in applications requiring efficient storage and transmission of 3D scenes, such as web-based viewers and mobile AR.
